about: hardline's layers, checked by tests/test_hardline_layering.py on every test run. Adopted from the reviewed map (scratch/review-2026-10-22/hardline-layers.json, at 1580c81) and brought to hardline 0.2: digests in the domain, the HTTP helpers and telemetry among the adapters, httpx2 and OpenTelemetry each confined to one file, no provider SDK. The format is that of slick crafting-aces' layer-check.py. 'why' keys are read by neither.
scan_why: Every Python file in the package. Tests are out of scan: a test root reaches adapters (the mock, a recording observer) by design.

why.stdlib: pure data and string work: structured.py parses JSON text and digests.py hashes canonical JSON; no clock, no I/O
why.pydantic: the one outside library admitted: the port's vocabulary is pydantic models, and validation is the domain's own rule
why.hardline.domain.*: the core types, errors and digests reach only each other; nothing here reaches the runtime, a port or an adapter
why.forbid: no I/O, no logging, no HTTP, no YAML, no telemetry in the core

why.split from domain: ModelRuntime lives under domain/, but it is the inside that calls the driven ports; a layer of its own keeps the core types on the narrower allowance
why.asyncio, time, random: the defaults of the injected sleep, clock and rng, and asyncio.timeout for the call's limits.seconds
why.logging: configuration warnings (shared_fate) and an observer that raised; the fallback signal is the CallObserver port, not a log line
why.hardline.domain.ports: the runtime names its driven ports: ModelBackend, SecretResolver, CallObserver

why.hardline.domain.types: a port is stated in domain types (ModelSpec, Request, RawCompletion, CallEvent)
why.no other port: not in allow, so a port reaching another port is a finding
why.forbid logging/opentelemetry: a port that traces forces that opinion on every implementor

why.*: an adapter's own technology: httpx2, yaml, os, pathlib, opentelemetry (each confined to one file by single_importer)
adapters build RawCompletion and raise BackendError, ConfigError, SecretError
why.the underscored helpers: shared by the provider adapters: one HTTP client policy, one status classifier, one options reader
why.not hardline.domain.ports: a backend satisfies ModelBackend structurally, so no adapter needs the port module
why.not composition, the runtime or a siblin: an adapter reaching the root or another technology is a finding

why.inspect: whether complete and aclose are coroutine functions
why.hardline.domain.ports, hardline.domain.t: the port it checks against, and the shapes a call must return
why.not an adapter or the root: it checks a backend it is handed, and names none

why.*: rich_click, json, sys, asyncio; importlib.resources in skill.py
why.hardline: the CLI reaches the public surface only. The map cannot allow the package root without every hardline.* path, so tests/test_hardline_layering.py also holds the CLI to names in hardline.__all__
why.forbid: naming a concrete adapter in the CLI is a second wiring

why.*, hardline: the composition root is the one place allowed to reach everything; the package __init__ re-exports the public surface

single_importer_why: one file per technology, its types handed out under hardline's own names (_http.Transport, otel.TracerProvider)
